elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: The rendered Article XXII now reads "NO RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL The Licensor shall have no right of first refusal or right to match." The original obligation on Licensee (Customer) to give written notice of any bona fide third-party asset-purchase or merger offer and to allow Licensor a five-business-day Exercise Period to take that offer is deleted, so no most-favoured-offer/matching mechanic in Vendor's favour survives in the operative text.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit no Customer-side MFN/right-to-match obligation exists at all (the only operative sentence is a negation of any Licensor first-refusal or matching right), so the scope condition has nothing to attach to.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the deleted grant carried the "During the term of this Agreement" duration; with the grant removed there is no surviving Customer MFN duration to limit.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no comparison or matching obligation remains on Licensee, so no like-for-like carve-out is required.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative grant of the Right of First Refusal/matching mechanic against Licensee is replaced with an express negation, so Customer carries no most-favoured-offer obligation benefiting Vendor.

Minimality is acceptable: only the Article XXII grant and the conditional opening of the follow-on sentence were touched; the one-line negation is a concise substitute for the deleted mechanic and adds no requirement outside the MFN checklist ("or right to match" merely restates the same deleted mechanic).

Intent fails on dangling antecedents. The retained sentence now reads "The Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party," but "the transaction" and "the third party" were introduced only in the deleted first paragraph (the bona fide third-party offer to purchase assets or merge). Repair by either deleting the follow-on sentence together with the grant, or restating it with its own antecedent, e.g. "Licensee may consummate any sale of all or substantially all of its assets, or any merger or consolidation, with a third party without any notice to, or first-refusal or matching right of, Licensor."

Intent also fails on a contradictory retained sentence. Stripped of its condition ("In the event the Licensor declines or fails to exercise... the Right of First Refusal"), the retained sentence reads as an unconditional Licensee right to consummate a third-party transaction, which conflicts with the retained Change of Control provision (p0134) and assignment provision (p0149) that still require Licensor consent. Add an express subordination (e.g. "subject to Article [Change of Control] and Article [Assignment]") or delete the sentence entirely.
